evidence.field: 就: 字形、早期用例與《說文》分析
evidence.text: CUHK interprets oracle-bone and bronze 就 forms as 亯 over 京: 亯 is read as a temple and 京 as a raised platform, yielding a proposed scene of ritual offering at height. It reports oracle-bone uses chiefly as place names; bronze uses include a verbal ‘complete/enlarge’ in 申就乃命 on the Shi Ke Xu, and ‘go to’ in the Warring States 鄂君啟車節 route list. It says Chu forms share strokes between 亯 and 京, while Qin slips show 京 + 尤, the form reflected in small seal. It also quotes the Eastern Han Shuowen definition ‘high’ and its analysis 从京从尤, while recording a Zhou-script form 𡰜. These are source analyses; the ritual interpretation and the relationship between early place-name graphs and later verbal uses are not settled by the entry.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：就

evidence.source: 陳致, 復旦大學出土文獻與古文字研究中心
evidence.field: early forms and competing readings, sections on 史惠鼎 and 鄂君啟車節
evidence.text: The author notes that most oracle-bone examples with 亯 + 京 are place names, not verbs; an older interpretation of one as 就庸 is discussed. A mid-Western Zhou 宰獸簋 phrase 申就乃命 is treated verbally with a sense near ‘complete.’ For the Shi Hui Ding 日就月將 inscription, the author argues the early form included 亯 + 京/high + 止; later 又/尤 forms may result from graphic confusion of 止. The article also discusses a Warring States use of 就 borrowed for 造 in travel contexts. These are arguments, including competing interpretations, rather than a settled account of all early forms and senses.
evidence.kind: scholarly paleographic argument with competing analyses
evidence.title: 陳致：“日居月諸”與“日就月將”：早期四言詩與祭祀禮辭釋例

evidence.field: 京: graph analysis and reported semantic history
evidence.text: The entry analyzes archaic 京 as a tall platform or tower, with the upper portion representing a structure and lower strokes its supports; it gives ‘large/high platform’ as the original sense and reports later place-name and capital uses. This supports 京 as a semantic/depictive element in the proposed early 就 scene; it does not establish the full graph's reading or formation independently.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：京

evidence.field: 尤: graph analysis, readings and semantic proposals
evidence.text: The entry reports a bronze shape analyzed as 又 plus a small extra stroke, proposed as a hand with a growth; it gives a proposed early sense ‘wart/lump’ and semantic developments including ‘unusual’ and ‘especially.’ It records the Shuowen account 異也，从乙，又聲. These claims illuminate the historical character 尤 but do not prove that 尤 was the lower part of the earliest 就 graphs.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：尤

evidence.field: Old Chinese reconstruction table, v1.1 (2014), rows for 尤 and 就
evidence.text: In the Baxter–Sagart 2014 notation, 尤 yóu is MC hjuw and OC *[ɢ]ʷə; 就 jiù is MC dzjuwH and OC *[dz]u[k]-s, glossed ‘go to.’ These entries do not furnish a close direct Old Chinese rhyme match that would independently demonstrate 尤 as the phonetic in 就. Their MC forms are source-data notation, not reconstructions.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1

evidence.text: The inspected entry gives Mandarin 京 as jīng. This is current reading metadata only, not evidence for an ancient sound relationship.

gaps: The early oracle-bone graphs are mostly reported as place names; whether they are the same lexeme as later verbal 就 is not established. The cited proposed interpretation 就庸 is a minority/older reading.

The relationship from proposed ‘ritual at height’ or ‘high’ to later ‘complete’ and ‘go to/approach’ is not demonstrated as a continuous semantic chronology. The cited uses should remain separate attestations rather than ordered glosses.

The earliest lower element is disputed: Fudan argues some early forms included 止 and that later 又/尤 forms may be graphic corruption; CUHK describes Qin slips with 京 + 尤. The Shuowen component analysis is historical testimony, not confirmation of the earliest structure.

The role of 尤 as phonetic in the later graph is not securely established by these sources. Baxter–Sagart gives 尤 *[ɢ]ʷə and 就 *[dz]u[k]-s; the sound comparison does not support a simple close match. No independently established pronunciation of a depicted object is relevant here because no whole-graph loan claim is adopted.

The local Baxter–Sagart and Unihan row metadata supplied in the dossier was not independently re-read from repository files in this invocation. Official Unicode U+4EAC, U+5C31 and U+5C24 pages were attempted and inaccessible; CUHK entries supplied current reading metadata but are not official Unihan records.

No glyph image was visually inspected. The CUHK image links identify candidate script-form examples but the database's reuse terms for those specific image assets were not verified, so no image is proposed. Xiaoxuetang's applicable CC0 notice was verified, but its exact 就 query/image could not be retrieved.

limitations.text: No image candidate met both identity and reuse-provenance requirements during this run. Commons searches returned unrelated character files. CUHK provides direct oracle and bronze glyph links on its 就 record, but reuse permission for those specific images was not established. Xiaoxuetang confirms CC0 1.0 for query-interface glyph images and glyph attributes, but its character-specific 就 query was inaccessible. Image pixels were not inspected.
